business_scope.primary_industry_name: Consumer Polling and Cross-Border Market Research Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Nacional), no sub-state tax or corporate registry distinctions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, por el que se transpone la normativa de la UE y se crea el Registro Central de Titularidades Reales.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales accessible to SEPBLAC, notaries, registrars and AML-obliged entities upon legitimate interest; not fully public)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the identification document (passport/national ID) of each shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of the signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of any non-resident corporate shareholder, including statutory corporate existence and registered legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry/chamber of commerce of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney or corporate resolution authorizing the incorporation of an SL, shareholder attendance and appointment of administrators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent corporate organ in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and risk-rating of politically exposed persons per Article 14 of Law 10/2010; mandatory screening against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists as transposed by EU Council Regulations, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List for USD transactions, and Spanish national sanction and counter-terrorism finance lists administered by SEPBLAC, AEAT and CNMV; enhanced due diligence is triggered by non-resident beneficial ownership, PEP status, or high-risk third-country ties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be expressed in Spanish/Castilian script; foreign alphabets and diacritic marks must be transliterated to standard Spanish characters; the legal form suffix 'Sociedad Limitada' or 'SL' is mandatory and may not be abbreviated in any other language; names must sufficiently distinguish the company from existing registered names and cannot be misleading as to activity or protected identifiers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of a final name rejection, an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) may be filed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice; a replacement application may be filed immediately through the Registro Mercantil Central online portal. Name reservations are valid for 180 days; extension for a further 90 days is available only upon justified request filed before expiration, otherwise a new negative name certificate must be obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for low-risk market research SaaS entities only if the virtual office consists of a dedicated physical address in Spain under a serviced office agreement, with mail handling, local correspondence, and a named local contact; a mere PO Box or a purely administrative address without any physical desk is rejected by the Registro Mercantil and AEAT for substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection is approximately 5% for a low-risk registered office, rising to 10-15% if the entity is flagged for reactive analysis, incomplete UBO filings, or recurrent discrepancies in annual filings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative company name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) - single application
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RMERC tariff, statutory fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the incorporation deed (escritura de constitución) including notary transcript, one authorized original, and UBO statement annex
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notario (Notary Public) in the registered office city
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (arancel notarial) based on capital, number of signatures and number of pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional NIF/CIF application before the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; included in incorporation process

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mercantile Registry registration entry for the SL, inscription of administrators, and deposit of the incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (in the province of the registered office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration arancel calculated on tax value and number of entries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/Hague legalization bundle for foreign shareholder/director documents and power of attorney (per set of up to three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / Justice and Foreign Affairs competent authority in the issuing country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing consular or apostille fee per document; market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT and UBO compliance advisory fee - preparation and coordination of UBO file, PEP/sanctions screening evidence, and pre-incorporation due diligence report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional service fee based on volume and cross-border complexity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Law (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital), including Articles 4, 20-23, 28-30, 32-35, 58-62, 159-204, 209-252, and 285-290; supplemented by the Commercial Registry Regulations (Real Decreto 1784/1996) and Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and CIRCE procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent registry is the Commercial Registry of the province where the registered office is located (Registro Mercantil Provincial), with prior name-clearance by the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the company bylaws and the required tax identification documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid upon incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. No general statutory escrow account is required, although a bank certificate of deposit may be used where the notary requires evidence of cash contribution. The amount shown is zero because Spain has no single fixed national state filing fee; notarial, registry, publication, municipal, and professional charges are variable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and ratifies the subscription and full payment of its issued shares by the founding shareholder as recorded in the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted for all statutory purposes; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, if a board structure is adopted, [names] are appointed directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal incompatibility; (4) [name] is appointed managing officer with authority to complete tax, banking, registry, employment, data-protection, and operational registrations; and (5) the officers are authorized to execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Clear and reserve the company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its official name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, ranked by preference, together with applicant identification and contact details. Obtain the negative name certificate. The certificate is generally valid for three months for notarial incorporation purposes and must be renewed if the deed is not executed within the applicable period.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or challenge the refusal through the registry's applicable administrative review procedure. Do not execute the deed until a valid certificate is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public and, where applicable, the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain Spanish tax identification numbers for non-resident founders, directors, and beneficial owners where required. Legalize or apostille foreign corporate documents and provide certified Spanish translations. Prepare powers of attorney in notarized form. Complete ultimate-beneficial-owner identification and anti-money-laundering screening before the notarial appointment.
required_dossiers: NIE or NIF documentation, as applicable
Foreign corporate certificate of incorporation and good standing
Foreign corporate bylaws and ownership chart
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation
Notarized power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing tax numbers, legalization, translations, or beneficial-owner evidence before the deed is signed. The notary may suspend execution until identification and source-of-funds requirements are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the incorporation deed and adopt bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public selected in the registered-office province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the name certificate, bylaws, founder details, capital subscription statement, registered office, corporate purpose, governance model, director appointments, and contribution evidence. Execute the public deed before the notary. For cash contributions, transfer the capital to the formation account or use the statutory founder declaration where legally acceptable and accepted by the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting defects in the deed or bylaws and re-execute the affected instrument. The notary must refuse or defer execution where mandatory corporate, identification, or anti-money-laundering requirements are incomplete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification and register the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency for NIF issuance; Provincial Commercial Registry for incorporation registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the provisional NIF using Form 036, then submit the notarized deed and bylaws to the Provincial Commercial Registry, electronically through the notary or through the registry filing channel. Pay the applicable notarial and registry charges. After registration, obtain the definitive NIF and file the updated Form 036.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry defect notice within the stated correction period, amend the deed or bylaws where necessary, and resubmit. An appeal or qualification challenge may be filed under the Commercial Registry Regulations if the defect is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete corporate governance and beneficial-owner books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry and the company registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalize the compulsory corporate books electronically, including the shareholders' register, minutes book, and, where relevant, contracts with the sole shareholder. Adopt the first board or sole-director resolution, confirm signing powers, approve the bank mandate, and maintain beneficial-owner records. File annual accounts and other mandatory corporate information within statutory deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify defective electronic legalization or filing through the Commercial Registry. Re-adopt resolutions where quorum, authority, signature, or conflict-of-interest requirements were not properly documented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, employment, data, and local operational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, Social Security Treasury, Spanish Data Protection Agency, relevant autonomous community, and municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the business activity and tax obligations through Form 036, enroll employees and the company with Social Security before employment begins, and assess GDPR obligations for consumer-panel and survey data. File the applicable municipal responsible declaration or obtain an activity licence for the premises. Register or notify any regulated sector activity only if the actual operating model triggers a specific rule.
required_dossiers: Privacy notice, data-processing records, and processor agreements
Municipal responsible declaration or activity licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to tax or municipal information requests, correct classification or premises documentation, and submit amended declarations. For data-protection matters, implement corrective measures and respond to any AEPD inquiry within its stated deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sector-specific industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for a consumer polling and cross-border market research SaaS platform. Premises-related controls are administered by the competent autonomous-community authority and the municipality where the office or technical installation is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No manufacturing or sector operating permit is ordinarily required. A municipal responsible declaration for the opening or commencement of a non-industrial office activity, or a municipal activity licence where required by local rules, may be necessary.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent autonomous-community environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from formal EIA for ordinary office-based market-research SaaS operations without industrial installations, significant emissions, hazardous waste, or material land-use impacts. Site-specific screening remains necessary for data centres, generators, cooling systems, or other regulated installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific process wastewater or VOC limits ordinarily apply to office operations. Discharge to public sewer must comply with municipal and autonomous-community requirements. Electronic equipment, batteries, packaging, and other waste must be managed through authorized waste operators under Spanish waste legislation. Any backup generator, refrigeration system, or industrial installation must comply with applicable air-emission, noise, refrigerant, and waste rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupation, verify municipal fire-safety and accessibility requirements, obtain any required responsible declaration or technical certificate, and ensure the premises satisfy the Spanish Building Code and applicable fire-protection rules. Structural load certification is required where the premises contain server equipment, storage, or alterations affecting loads. Implement occupational risk prevention, emergency planning, electrical safety, and workplace health measures under Law 31/1995 and related regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Provincial and regional tax bodies have no corporate tax competence; the Basque Country and Navarra operate separate foral regimes only for entities with principal establishments there.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Obtain a provisional NIF for the company from AEAT using Modelo 036 before executing the incorporation deed. Step 2 - Execute the public deed before a Spanish notary and file the deed with the Registro Mercantil. Step 3 - Within one month of incorporation, file Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive corporate NIF (NIF-CIF) and simultaneously register for IVA (VAT) and IAE. Step 4 - Non-resident shareholders/parent entities must obtain their own non-resident NIF via Modelo 036/030 and, if applicable, appoint a Spanish tax representative. Step 5 - Deliver the ultimate beneficial owner declaration and maintain a local registered office and a Spanish bank account; if the SL is in a regulated sector, certifications are filed with the tax or supervisory authority as required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is tax-resident under art. 8 LIS because it is incorporated under Spanish law. Worldwide income is subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (CIT); general rate 25%; newly created trading entities may apply 15% to profits of the first two tax periods under art. 29.3 LIS. No pass-through election exists in Spanish domestic law; the entity is treated as a separate taxable person for CIT and IVA. Territorial_Scope: worldwide taxation with foreign tax credit; not a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity unless specifically authorised in the Zona Especial Canaria.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election. Available elections: (i) consolidated tax group regime (arts. 64-70 LIS) for resident groups with direct/indirect holding of at least 70% and unanimous shareholder election; (ii) reduced 15% CIT rate for newly created trading entities in the first two profitable periods; (iii) corporate tax credits for R&D+i and employment; (iv) ETVE holding company regime for EU/third-country shareholding management; (v) voluntary SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) filing; (vi) OSS (One-Stop-Shop) election for intra-EU distance sales and B2C digital services under the EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold; (vii) anti-hybrid rules under art. 15 LIS apply mandatorily to neutralise mismatches, with no domestic hybrid election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish VAT, implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC); Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla are outside Spanish VAT and apply IGIC/IPSI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: any business habitually carrying out taxable supplies in Spanish territory must register for IVA before commencing activity. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C telecommunications/broadcasting/digital services supplied from Spain, the OSS registration threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year (below the threshold, supplies remain taxable in the Member State of establishment). The Régimen Simplificado is available to small traders with turnover below EUR 250,000 but does not waive registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time clearance via SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) is mandatory for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,000,000, for VAT groups, and for non-established businesses using the EU refund procedure; SII requires electronic submission of invoice records to AEAT within 4 business days via web services/API (8 days for third-party issued invoices). All B2G invoicing uses Facturae format through FACe. Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) will make electronic invoicing mandatory for all businesses after the implementing regulation is enacted, which is still pending; Regulation 1007/2023 (VeriFactu) mandates certified billing software with integrity, traceability and QR/hash features from 2025. Spain does not apply fiscal stamping or pre-clearance of individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under art. 21 LIVA if the goods physically leave EU customs territory and the exporter is the Spanish entity. For the market research/SaaS platform, exports of services to non-Spanish taxable persons (B2B) are outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rule (art. 69 LIVA); services to non-EU non-taxable persons (B2C) are also outside the scope when effectively used in a third country. Zero-rating under arts. 21-22 LIVA applies to services directly linked to exported goods and to certain international services. The SL must substantiate the customer's status and country, the nature of the service, and the actual export/receipt abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Modelo DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) - customs export declaration with exit confirmation and NRE (Número de Referencia de Exportación)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR showing Spanish port/airport of exit and non-EU destination
Commercial invoice with Incoterm, full value, product/service description, destination, and export VAT exemption clause (Bienes exportados exentos - art. 21 LIVA)
Packing list and export licences for dual-use or restricted goods (if applicable)
Proof of payment / SWIFT MT103 (inward remittance) evidencing receipt of funds in the Spanish bank account of the SL
For cross-border services: signed contract, customer certificate of fiscal residence, and description of the actual place of use/benefit
Intrastat declarations when intra-EU dispatches exceed EUR 400,000 per calendar year
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retrospectively withdraw the 0% rate and assess 21% VAT on the invoice value plus late-payment interest if the export documentation is incomplete, the goods do not leave the EU, or the inward remittance is not received within the 180-day conformity period. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the VAT determined under arts. 170-171 LIVA, and the four-year limitation period allows clawback of prior periods. Falsifying export documents or creating fictitious exports may constitute a criminal offence under art. 305 Código Penal where the evaded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 1-5 years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount; the tax assessment and penalty can be extended where concealment is shown, and the audit defence requires full availability of the DUA, transport evidence, payment evidence and contracts for the entire limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); for foreign-investment and statistical exchange-control matters, the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCEI) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation acts as the competent foreign-exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a euro-area member state and applies full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions under EU Treaty principles and Royal Decree 1816/1991. The euro is freely convertible. There are no exchange-control restrictions on inward direct investment, foreign borrowing, or profit remittance. Dividends, interest, royalties, and liquidation proceeds may be repatriated through the Spanish banking system, subject only to standard tax documentation, corporate income tax/IRNR withholding obligations, transfer pricing substantiation, and AML/KYC verification. No prior Bank of Spain authorization is required for ordinary commercial payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender requirement exists in Spain. Exporters and service providers are not required to convert foreign currency proceeds into euro, hold them in a designated account, or repatriate them within a statutory timeline. EU and Spanish law permit free retention and disposition of export proceeds in any permitted currency. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations and customs/foreign-transaction documentation may apply above the applicable reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as a supplementary payment rail, but medium legal acceptability as the sole treasury relationship. EU-licensed electronic-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions may operate in Spain through cross-border passporting under PSD2 after communicating with the Banco de España. Offshore or non-EEA EMIs, including UK-only authorised firms after Brexit, generally require a Spanish branch or separate Spanish/EEA authorisation to provide payment services to Spanish-domiciled corporate clients. Wise and PayPal can be used for mass-payout functionality, but final settlement and statutory corporate cash management should remain in a Spanish bank account in the name of the ES_SL entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance of the legal representative, managing director, or appointed attorney is generally required for the account-opening interview under Spanish AML regulations. Remote onboarding may be accepted by some tier-1 banks if video identification and qualified electronic signature are used and the company is verifiable in the Spanish Mercantile Registry. Foreign directors should be prepared to appoint one local authorised signatory with a NIE and a notarised, apostilled power of attorney; physical presence of that Spanish-appointed representative will be the most efficient way to satisfy the bank's KYC interview mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a non-resident shareholder without a clear corporate resolution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Spanish deed of capital increase or shareholder contribution, current Mercantile Registry certificate, shareholder ledger, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, bank reference letter, source-of-wealth statement, memorandum of deposit, and the foreign investor's tax/corporate registry extract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mass payout pattern to many low-value consumer panel respondents across multiple countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed consumer consent forms, platform terms and conditions, survey panel participant agreements, reward programme rules, payment calculations, ISO 20022 batch file samples, geolocation/IP-check logs, sanctions and PEP screening evidence, and a written AML risk assessment for the payout model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reported revenue from market research SaaS not substantiated by export invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer subscription agreements, usage analytics, service delivery reports, export invoices with adequate business purpose codes, bank statements showing collection from end clients, and transfer pricing documentation supporting the commercial margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity due to layered non-resident holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full group structure chart, certificates of good standing for each holding entity, copies of constitutional documents, shareholder registers, legal opinion on control and ownership, and a signed 'titular real' declaration acceptable to the Spanish bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from jurisdictions perceived as high-risk for AML purposes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts describing the legitimate service, due diligence on the counterparty, business justification for the jurisdiction, sanctions-screening certificate, enhanced due diligence questionnaire, and evidence that the transaction is fully recorded in the statutory accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party EMI payment processors instead of direct Spanish banking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of the EMI licence or payment institution authorisation, FCA/other regulatory register extract, PSD2 passporting confirmation, contractual flow-of-funds diagrams, segregation of client funds evidence, and bank confirmation that the EMI is on-boarded as a permitted payment service provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA inbound transfers or a SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA transfers. The payment should be directed to the ES_SL operational account or dedicated capital contribution account with the Spanish bank; field 70 must reference 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection', the corporate resolution number, and the notarial deed reference. The sending bank should be instructed to use the appropriate balance-of-payments purpose code for inward direct investment. After receipt, the Spanish entity should file any required foreign-investment statistical declaration with the DGCEI if the non-resident investor’s stake meets the applicable threshold. Verification of the source of funds is supported by the deed, shareholder resolution, audited financial statements, and confirmations from the remitting bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro-denominated disbursements within SEPA, use SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001). For non-euro cross-border payments, use SWIFT MT103 with the proper commercial purpose code, including if needed a certificate of payment under Spanish foreign-transaction reporting rules. For larger or documentary settlements, commercial letters of credit (UCP600) and documentary collections are permissible. For the platform’s consumer-panel rewards, PayPal Mass Payout and Wise Business provide batch and API-driven clearing rails with local-currency payout capability; any such outflow must be reconcilable to the platform’s participant ledger and subject to sanctions/PEP screening before transmission.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted Latin American currencies
Interest rate swaps incidental to cross-currency funding and treasury management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposito de Cuentas Anuales (Annual Accounts Deposit: balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, and statutory notes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial / Registro Mercantil Central (Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within 6 months of fiscal year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year end); deposit with the Commercial Registry within 1 month of approval, i.e. no later than 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Registry closure of the company's file (cierre registral) after two consecutive years of non-deposit; refusal to register corporate resolutions until accounts are filed; administrative fines from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; joint and several liability of directors for damages caused by failure to file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 200 - Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) including annual tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT - Spanish Tax Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1-25 July for calendar-year taxpayers (within 25 calendar days following the expiration of the 6-month period after the tax year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge under LGT Article 27: 5% per month for the first 3 months, then 10%, 15% and up to 20%; late payment interest at statutory rates; penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax due if AEAT issues an assessment; criminal prosecution under Criminal Code Article 310 for intentional non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Titularidad Real (annual confirmation and update of the ultimate beneficial owners register) - required at incorporation, within 10 business days of any ownership change, and reconfirmed during the annual corporate cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil and Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (central UBO register under Ley 6/2023)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 business days of any modification to shareholdings or control chain; annual alignment with the ordinary shareholders' meeting and annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under AML Law 10/2010: EUR 600-10,000 for minor infractions and EUR 10,000-60,000 for serious infractions; suspension of acceptance of Commercial Registry filings until the UBO records are updated

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 - Annual declaration of third-party transactions (clients, panel payees, suppliers, and other counterparties exceeding EUR 3,005.06 per counterpart in a calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT - Spanish Tax Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1-28 February of the year following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Flat fines under LGT Articles 198-199 ranging from EUR 150 to EUR 20,000 depending on the number of omitted or inaccurate data records; lower fines if corrected voluntarily before notification

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where at least two of the following three criteria are exceeded on two consecutive balance sheet dates: (i) total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; (iii) average number of employees exceeds 50. Audit is also mandatory for listed entities, credit and financial institutions, and entities whose parent company prepares consolidated EU-IFRS accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP per Plan General de Contabilidad (Real Decreto 1514/2007, amended by Real Decreto 1159/2010 and Real Decreto 1/2021); SME abridged formats (PGC Pymes) available to entities below the audit thresholds; EU-endorsed IFRS compulsory for consolidated accounts of listed groups. Commercial books must be retained for 6 years (Código de Comercio art. 30), tax documentation for 10 years (LGT art. 66); schema-standard statutory retention value set to 7 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain a dedicated UBO register and file the Declaración de Titularidad Real with the Registro Mercantil at incorporation and within 10 business days of every transfer of participaciones or change in the control chain. The management body must reconfirm the UBO record as part of the ordinary annual accounts cycle, documenting the full name, national identification, percentage of participation, and nature of control. All share transfers, even at par value, must be entered in the Libro Registro de Socios and communicated to the Commercial Registry before annual filings are accepted. The Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (Ley 6/2023) centralizes verified UBO data for access by member state financial intelligence units.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Consejeros / appointments recorded in corporate minute book)
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titulares Reales)
Registered share transfer ledgers and pledge records on participaciones (when applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400-1,500 per year (EUR 350-1,400) for a Madrid or Barcelona registered office address, mail handling, and professional agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000-12,000 per engagement (EUR 4,500-11,000) for a small-to-mid SL subject to a full statutory audit; zero audit fee applies if the SME exemption thresholds are satisfied

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, general rate, Ley 27/2014 art. 29.1)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created SL companies enjoy 15% reduced rate on the taxable base for the first two tax years with positive taxable base after formation (art. 29.1 LIS), subject to the minimum tax floor. Additional reliefs include: R&D and technological innovation tax credits of 25% to 42% (art. 35 LIS), patent box exemption of 50% of qualifying IP income (art. 23? LIS), and the capitalisation reserve (reserva de capitalización) reducing the tax base by 10% of retained profit increases, capped at 10% of the positive taxable base. Standard digital-market-research SaaS revenue (subscriptions, survey panel payments) does not qualify for the Canary Islands ZEC regime unless the activity is physically relocated to Gran Canaria, Tenerife, La Palma, Lanzarote or Fuerteventura.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward (no statutory expiry, art. 26 LIS); annual offset is capped at 70% of the positive tax base for companies with net turnover below EUR 20 million; 50% for turnover between EUR 20 million and EUR 60 million; 25% for turnover exceeding EUR 60 million (art. 26.1 second paragraph LIS, as amended by Law 11/2021).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); mandatory electronic filing through the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) electronic headquarters using an authorised electronic certificate (e.g. FNMT user certificate, electronic DNI, or representation registration).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; also follow annual filing of financial statements with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, filing window runs from 1 to 25 July of the following year. General statutory rule: file within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax period end (art. 124 LIS). A foreign-owned SL with a permanent establishment in Spain files the same Modelo 200 on the PE's Spanish-sourced accounting results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration type code: '1' for ordinary declaration within the deadline, '3' for complementary declaration in response to a correction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owner/shareholder: this box records the filer as the Spanish-resident entity; a non-resident PE branch files as a separate taxpayer with PE-specific code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) of the SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NIF must correspond to the Spanish entity's tax ID; non-resident companies operating through a PE use the PE's assigned NIF with suffix.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name (razón social) exactly as registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE, insert the foreign parent's name followed by 'Establecimiento Permanente en España'.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the tax period; tax period cannot exceed 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE branch in Spain is normally aligned with the Spanish calendar year unless the parent's accounting year is formally different.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before tax (resultado contable del ejercicio) per the profit and loss account prepared under Spanish GAAP (PGC 2007).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE accounting result must comply with Spanish commercial law for branch accounts; intra-branch charges require arm's length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments: Box 104 records increases (non-deductible expenses such as sanctions, amortisation excess, related-party interest above threshold); Box 105 records decreases (dividend participation exemption, capitalisation reserve, prior R&D credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Permanent adjustments must respect source rules; intra-group dividend flows from the foreign parent may be excluded only where the participation exemption is individually claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting taxable base (base imponible) after adjustments and loss-offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE taxable base for Spanish-source income must be allocated under OECD profit attribution principles; the parent's foreign results are not included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax payable (cuota íntegra) at 25% before credits and withholdings, subject to the 15% rate for newly created SLs where eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty rates and foreign tax credits are applied at the later boxes for credits and payments; no foreign tax credit for taxes attributable to exempt foreign source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net withholding and prepayments of the year: Modelo 202 instalments paid, plus any Spanish-source withholding tax suffered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE branch payments to the Spanish parent or to the PE's head office are not deductible and no withholding arises on branch profits under domestic law beyond the PE profits tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting tax payable (cuota diferencial) or refund claimed after deductions and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE must settle the final balance in EUR via direct debit (domiciliación) or through the electronic bank payment gateway of AEAT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior tax-office request triggers 'recargos por presentación extemporánea' under art. 27 LGT: 5% surcharge if the return is filed within 3 months after the deadline; 10% if within 3-6 months; 15% if within 6-12 months; and 20% plus late-payment interest if later. Where the tax authority formally requires the return first, the fine ranges from EUR 150 to EUR 6,000. Understatement leading to tax loss is characterised as a 'grave' infraction (art. 191 LGT) with a 50% penalty, or 100% with deliberate or proven concealment. Interest on late payment is 3.75% annually for the period of delay.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 / Modelo 222 (pagos fraccionados) submitted electronically through AEAT; Modelo 222 is mandatory only for taxpayers with net turnover exceeding EUR 10 million in the prior year; otherwise Modelo 202 applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalment payments: April, October and December (three instalments per fiscal year based on the prior year's assessed base or the actual accounting profit method).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments must be filed within the first 20 calendar days of April (first instalment), October (second instalment), and December (third instalment); for a calendar-year SL the first payment is due 1-20 April, the second 1-20 October, the third 1-20 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE branches use the PE NIF; the instalment is computed on the Spanish PE base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period year for which the instalment is paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments are mandatory for PEs deriving Spanish-source business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Instalment tax base: 18% of the accounting profit for the first three, nine and eleven months of the current year, or 25% applied to the prior-year tax base under the general method; actual-profit method is the default for SMEs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs must use the same method chosen in Modelo 200; no asset-based methods apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting amount payable to the Treasury.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is made in euros from a Spanish bank account; online payment via AEAT 'Pago de impuestos' service.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment or late payment of instalments triggers the same extemporaneous surcharge scale of art. 27 LGT (5%-20%) plus 3.75% late-payment interest. Failure to declare instalments without payment is also subject to the art. 191 LGT penalty of up to 50% of the amount avoided (implying that the instalment payment is not a mere deposit but a substantive obligation).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders under the Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, art. 25.1.e TRLIRNR; rate set by Ley 5/2020). For EU/EEA shareholders holding at least 5% of the SL's capital for more than 12 consecutive months, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) provides a 0% withholding rate, subject to evidence of residence and no abuse. Domestic distributions to Spanish residents are subject to 19% personal income tax withholding at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty (CDI - Convenio para Evitar la Doble Imposición), the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Spanish paying entity a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (certificado de residencia fiscal) issued by the treaty-state tax authority covering the payment year. The certificate must be submitted before the payment date so that the reduced rate is applied at source; where excess withholding has already been applied, the non-resident must file a refund application via Modelo 210 (IRNR) within the general four-year prescription period, accompanying a TRC bearing an apostille or legalisation plus an official Spanish translation if the certificate is not bilingual (Spanish/English). Procedural steps: (i) obtain TRC in the residence state; (ii) file Form 23 or the simplified procedure with AEAT for the application of the treaty at source; (iii) report the payment on Modelo 200 of the Spanish SL and on the annual Modelo 193/123 informative returns; (iv) for EU parents, additionally complete the 'residencia fiscal en la UE/EEE' declaration and the anti-abuse substance questionnaire when the shareholding was acquired from a related party.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalties: 24% gross withholding on Spanish-source IP royalties paid to non-residents (art. 25.1.f TRLIRNR). Treaty rates generally range from 0% to 10% (e.g., US-Spain 8%; UK-Spain 10%; Germany-Spain 5%); the EU Interest & Royalty Directive grants a 0% rate on qualifying cross-border royalties between associated EU companies satisfying a 25% shareholding for at least 24 months. Statutory interest: 19% on Spanish-source interest paid to non-residents (art. 25.1.d TRLIRNR); treaties commonly reduce to 5% or 10%, with 0% under the EU Interest & Royalty Directive. Payments from a Spanish SL to its foreign shareholder for a trademark, platform software licence or internal debt must comply with arm's length documentation or they will be recharacterised as constructive dividends, triggering 19% dividend withholding in addition to the 24%/19% base rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory when the Spanish taxpayer's net turnover in the preceding tax period reaches EUR 45 million or the total related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period (arts. 18.3 and 18.8 LIS, RD 634/2015). Entities below these thresholds remain obliged to document each controlled transaction on a transactional file kept on request (art. 18.2 LIS). For a consumer-panel SaaS platform, the typical controlled transactions are: (i) payment processing fees charged by an Amazon/Wise/PayPal affiliate; (ii) data-cloud hosting services from a related entity; (iii) commission payments to affiliated market-research sub-contractors; and (iv) shareholder loans. All must be evidenced by policy-level documentation showing the pricing benchmark.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies no standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' in the Gulf-style sense, but the substance-over-form doctrine is codified in art. 15 LGT (conflicto en la aplicación de la norma tributaria), the general anti-abuse rule (art. 13? and GAAR), the CFC rules of arts. 100-108 LIS, and the principal-purpose test (PPT) included in OECD-based DTAs. A consumer-panel survey platform must demonstrate real economic substance in Spain: local headcount with research and data-analytics functions, local contracts with panel respondents, Spanish premises or sub-leased favourable space, actual decision-making on pricing and data processing, and bank accounts in Spain. Where an SL claims treaty benefits or the participation exemption on foreign dividends, AEAT may deny the benefit if the entity lacks sufficient substantive presence; in a Spanish court of law the burden of proving economic substance falls on the taxpayer. For holding companies of IP (not the case here), the ETVE regime (art. 21 LIS) additionally imposes a substance requirement of a minimum of one full-time director and an office in Spain.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion (delito contra la Hacienda Pública)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting taxable income (e.g., undeclared cross-border subscription revenue from the consumer-panel platform) or fraudulently claiming non-existent expenses, where the resulting loss to the Spanish Treasury exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period before application of any offset.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prison sentence of 1 to 5 years plus a fine of six times the defrauded amount (arts. 305 and 305 bis of the Spanish Criminal Code). Where the fraud exceeds EUR 600,000 or the offence was committed through an organised network or false invoicing, the prison term is 2 to 6 years and the court may order closure of the business for up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SL who consent to or direct the concealment are personally liable as 'cooperadores necesarios' and jointly and severally liable for fines and civil restitution. Criminal courts may order disqualification from obtaining public subsidies, tax benefits or public contracts for up to 6 years, and they may impose a travel ban on EU/EEA movement? (preventive travel restriction) pending trial. Spanish criminal jurisdiction follows the foreign director if the offence is planned in Spain, and the legal entity itself may be prosecuted under art. 310 bis CP with penalties of up to 5 times the fine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / abuse-of-law (conflicto en la aplicación de la norma)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming the SL merely as an invoice conduit to channel Spanish market-research commissions to a low-tax jurisdiction, or claiming the 15% reduced rate on newly created companies while the real business is conducted from a foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT recharacterises the transaction under art. 15 LGT, computing the tax due as legally applicable to the real substance and imposing a specific penalty of 50% of the resulting tax base (art. 206 bis LGT). Interest at 3.75% accrues on the recharacterisation amount. Aggravating circumstances may raise the penalty to 100%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are derivatively liable for the tax debt when, acting in bad faith, they failed to exercise proper diligence in avoiding tax abuse (art. 43.2 LGT). In egregious cases, foreign directors may be barred from Spain's Golden Visa/Digital Nomad Visa regimes and may face a re-entry embargo for unpaid assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation failure and non-arm's-length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare a Local File/Master File when the EUR 45 million turnover or EUR 250,000 intra-group transaction threshold is exceeded, or applying an artificial 30% profit margin to the Spanish platform while the foreign parent is under-compensated for its functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT assesses an upward taxation adjustment to the Spanish tax base plus 3.75% late-payment interest. Under art. 18.13 LIS, the penalty for absent or incomplete documentation is EUR 1,500 per data item or set of data with a minimum of EUR 15,000? (in practice, ERP practice); a deliberate manipulation of prices can involve the general infraction penalty of 50% of the adjustment (art. 191 LGT).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board of the SL bears personal residual liability if it authored the intercompany contracts that produced the tax base shift. Spanish jurisprudence has pierced the veil to attach the foreign parent's assets in Spain when the SL is domiciled, managed and controlled as a wholly owned instrument of a US/EU parent, making directors personally liable for the assessed difference.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold on outbound payments (IRNR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest or royalties to a foreign shareholder or licensor without withholding the 19%/24%/19% statutory rates and without obtaining a valid TRC; also paying out platform commissions to non-resident survey respondents as if they were personal income without a NIF and without reporting on Modelo 123/193.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL is substituted as the accountable taxpayer (retenedor) and AEAT requires payment of the unwithheld amounts plus interest and the full 50% infraction penalty under art. 191 LGT (or 100% in cases of concealment). A fine of EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 may also be imposed per omitted form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under art. 42.2.b) LGT, directors are jointly and severally liable in cases of wilful failure to withhold by a company that lacks sufficient assets to pay. A foreign director with assets in Spain (e.g., a bank account, a property or the shareholding of the SL) may face attachment and a prohibition on leaving Spain during the enforcement procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving survey-panel 'incentive' payments in cash or through unlicensed e-money channels, paying fake panel members with no real data-collection activity, or converting revenue into cryptoassets through non-Spanish intermediaries to avoid enforcement of Spanish social security or VAT obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial and administrative infractions under Law 10/2010 carry fines up to EUR 150,000 for serious breaches and EUR 5,000,000 plus potential criminal consequences for money laundering under art. 301 CP (1 to 6 years' imprisonment and fines of treble the laundered value). The Bank of Spain may suspend the platform's operations for up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Court-imposed travel bans, property embargoes and bank-account freezing orders are routine against directors of the SL; judges may order personal surrender of passports for repeat offenders. Since the platform uses PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, any flow of funds to sanctioned jurisdictions or to shells holding credentials causes immediate extraterritorial exposure and the SL's directors are personally exposed to anti-money-laundering enforcement from Spain's SEPBLAC and the criminal courts.
